clue.text: Style that's plain, no question about it? On the contrary

indicators.note: the surface says the no-question pair goes around the plain word; on the contrary means the plain word goes around them instead

parts.note: plain means bare, unadorned
O is the figure nought, read as no or nothing

explanation.surface: A plain style that leaves no question about it, or perhaps exactly the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about it? On the contrary' turns the stated container round: the plain word goes around the no-question pair, not the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque is an ornate period style in art, architecture and music, the very opposite of plain.

clue.text: Shakespeare's all-round reputation

parts.note: in As You Like It the soldier seeks a reputation that Shakespeare calls by the name of a round, fragile thing that bursts

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's soldier seeks 'the bubble reputation', a fame as empty and short-lived as a soap globule.

clue.text: Picking up fruit-tree I left to fall back

indicators.note: in a down answer, picking up means lifting, so the letters read upwards
the letter I has left, so it is taken out

parts.note: an espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall or frame

explanation.surface: A gardener picks fruit from a tree and then sinks back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes I from ESPALIER to give ESPALER, and 'Picking up' turns that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slip back into a former worse state, such as illness.

clue.text: A hundred pennies drop: the game is up!

parts.note: a quid is British slang for a pound, which is a hundred pennies
to ditch something is to drop or abandon it

explanation.surface: The penny drops and someone realises the game is up.
explanation.walkthrough: The game in Harry Potter is played on broomsticks, high up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Quidditch is the airborne broomstick game in Harry Potter, so it is literally a game that is up.

clue.text: What's placed by plate? Resignation, sadly

indicators.note: sadly here means badly, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A gloomy resignation, with a question about the table setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating irons is a jocular term for cutlery, which is laid beside a dinner plate.

clue.text: All delivered after capture

parts.note: post- is the Latin prefix meaning after, as in postwar
to bag something is to catch or capture it

explanation.surface: A remark that everything was delivered once something was captured.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the whole batch of letters delivered to someone at one time.

clue.text: Announced best film

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so a word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the pick of something is the best of it

explanation.surface: The winner for best film is announced.
explanation.definitionFit: Pic is an informal word for a film or movie, as in the trade paper Variety.

clue.text: Way to eat some weeks, having chips in

indicators.note: the way word eats the other, taking it inside

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
Mar is short for March, a month lasting some weeks

explanation.surface: A diet plan for a few weeks that includes chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' suggests fried potatoes, but these are microchips, as in a smart card.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart device or card is one with microchips built in to give it computing power.

clue.text: Mixer in litres taken in drunken spree

indicators.note: the litres letter is taken in by the spree word, inside it

parts.note: a bender is a bout of heavy drinking

explanation.surface: A drinker downs litres of mixers on a binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixer' suggests a drink to add to spirits, but it is the kitchen appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender is a kitchen appliance that mixes or purées food.

clue.text: Marine mammal's elegance taking fish in sound

indicators.note: in sound means as heard, so the phrase is spoken and heard as the answer

parts.note: grace is elegance, and taking on an eel, a fish, gives grace-eel

explanation.surface: A seal gracefully catches a fish in a stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' could be a strait of water, fitting the seal, but it signals a soundalike: grace-eel said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey seal is a large seal of North Atlantic coasts, a marine mammal; the 's is read as is.

clue.text: Moved by gravity, lake is flowing into sea

indicators.note: the lake and the word is flow into the sea, so they sit inside its name

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea of northern Europe
L is a standard map abbreviation for lake
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lake drains under gravity into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballistic projectile, once launched, travels under the force of gravity alone.

clue.text: A mark to scrub for Eisenstein's maid

parts.note: dele is the proofreader's mark meaning delete, so a mark telling the printer to scrub something

explanation.surface: A maid is given a mark telling her to scrub something.
explanation.walkthrough: In Strauss's operetta Die Fledermaus, Adele is the chambermaid to Gabriel von Eisenstein, not the film director.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is the maid in the household of Eisenstein, a character in Strauss's Die Fledermaus.

clue.text: Oil, say, I had put on part of face

indicators.note: in an across answer, putting one piece on another means placing it after it

parts.note: the lip is part of the face
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone says they put some oil on their face.
explanation.definitionFit: Oils and fats are lipids, so oil is an example of the class of compounds.

clue.text: During organised day in Rome, pressure for minimum ups and downs

indicators.note: the pressure letter comes during the word for organised, sitting inside it

parts.note: neat means tidy and organised
P is the symbol for pressure in physics
the Ides was a day in the ancient Roman calendar, the 15th or 13th of the month

explanation.surface: On a well-planned Roman holiday, someone is pressured to keep the highs and lows to a minimum.
explanation.definitionFit: Neap tides occur at quarter moon and have the smallest range between high and low water.

clue.text: Conan Doyle's behind a bit of capital that's raised

definitions.text: a bit of capital that's raised

parts.note: Arthur was Conan Doyle's first name, so Arthur's means his
seat is a word for the behind or buttocks

explanation.surface: A remark about the writer's rear end, raised above the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur's Seat is a hill overlooking Edinburgh, the Scottish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur's Seat is an extinct volcano rising above Edinburgh, so it is a raised part of a capital city.

clue.text: Erect radar site at sea, where access can be controlled

indicators.note: at sea means in confusion, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A radar station is built out at sea, somewhere entry is restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like the location of the site but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A restricted area is a zone where entry is limited to authorised people.

clue.text: Give pounds to old sculptor

parts.note: to donate is to give
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra, and doubling it makes the plural, as pp does for pages

explanation.surface: Money is handed over to an aged sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was a Florentine Renaissance sculptor, famous for his bronze David.

clue.text: One sent to cover unsatisfactory private road

parts.note: off can mean not up to standard, as in an off day
a drive is a private road leading to a house

explanation.surface: A poor stretch of private road gets resurfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, cover is a fielding position on the off side, so an off drive is a shot hit towards it.
explanation.definitionFit: An off drive is a cricket stroke struck to the off side, often towards the cover fielder.

clue.text: Subversive addition to quartet of writers?

definitions.meaning: a subversive is a traitor working within
read literally, a fifth person who writes a column joins four others

explanation.surface: A subversive figure is added to a group of four writers.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifth columnist is a member of a hidden group working to undermine a nation from within.

clue.text: French clown once very worried

parts.note: antic is an archaic word for a clown or buffoon

explanation.surface: A French clown of years gone by was in a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means wild with anxiety, so it fits very worried.

clue.text: Substitute's reputation not good

indicators.note: not good means the good letter is left out

parts.note: standing is reputation or status

explanation.surface: A stand-in's reputation is said to be poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is someone who substitutes for another, as in theatre or film.

clue.text: Pure speed about to go to the head

indicators.note: the about letter goes to the head of the speed word, before it in a down answer

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
haste means speed

explanation.surface: Speed is said to have gone to someone's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure in the sense of morally clean and abstaining.

clue.text: A couple of points fixed as I desire

indicators.note: fixed means rearranged or sorted, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has a couple of things put right just as they wish.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaeresis is the two-dot mark placed over a vowel, as in naïve.

clue.text: Wine lifts atmosphere, around one March

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting means turning upwards, so the letters read backwards
the atmosphere word goes around the other piece

parts.note: air is the atmosphere
Jo is one of the March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: Wine lifts the mood around one day in March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is the family surname in Little Women; 'lifts' reads the assembled container upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Dismiss as valueless ultimate in hot spots

indicators.note: the ultimate letter in a word is its last one

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a heat rash as nothing to worry about.
explanation.definitionFit: To trash something is to condemn it as worthless, as in trashing a film.

clue.text: The start -literally, of Troilus and Cressida?

definitions.meaning: the opening part of a piece of music or writing
the Prologue of Shakespeare's play opens with the words 'In Troy', so its first five letters literally begin it

explanation.surface: A question about how Shakespeare's play begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida opens with a Prologue beginning 'In Troy, there lies the scene', so its very first letters spell the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is short for introduction, the opening section of a work.

clue.text: Bars of music at last in Chopin's works

indicators.note: the last letter of music goes in the word for Chopin's works

parts.note: Chopin wrote a famous set of 24 preludes for piano

indicators.note: the letter at the last position of a word is its final one

explanation.surface: Bars of music turning up at the very end of Chopin's pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like musical bars, but it is the verb meaning prevents.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to rule it out, so precludes means prevents or bars.

clue.text: Dog needs a clean up

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a mop is a quick clean, as in giving the floor a mop

explanation.surface: A dog needs cleaning up after itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pom is short for a Pomeranian, a small fluffy breed of dog.

clue.text: To cry is not right any more

parts.note: ex- describes something no longer so, read with 'is not' as a right that is no longer held
a claim is a right or title to something

explanation.surface: A complaint that a right no longer exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not ... any more' is split around 'right', so the former-state prefix wraps the clue word it comes before.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, so the verb matches to cry.

clue.text: Easily defeat in recount that's ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A recount ordered after an election produces a landslide.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce an opponent is to beat them heavily and convincingly.
